title: What haruspex generate or haruspex check reports with --format json
description: One document on standard output for a whole run. Version 1. A field may be added without a new version; one is removed, renamed or given another meaning only with a new version, so a tool checks "version". Paths are relative to the working directory when they are below it, with / between names on every platform. docs/command-line.md describes each field.

exitCode.description: The run's exit code, as the process exits with: 0 success, 1 failed, 2 a usage error, 3 an internal fault.

refused.description: Why no module ran: options that can't go together, --all finding nothing, two modules sharing an output folder. Empty when the modules ran.

modules.description: Each module's report, in the order they ran: one, or one for each config file --config names or --all finds.

config.description: The config file --config named or --all found; null when the run looked for one.

out.description: The output folder, once settled; null when the run failed before, or when check compared the module with its baseline alone (a baseline that is the output folder's own IR).

baseline.description: The baseline check judged the module against (--baseline, or "baseline" in the config file); null when there was none.

typed.description: What the module types; null when the run failed before inferring.

written.description: The files generate wrote, the IR first; empty for check and for a run that wrote nothing.

removed.description: The files generate removed: those its list (haruspex.files.json) named from the last run that this run didn't write. Empty for check.

unknowns.description: The module's unknowns, counted by reason, most first; null when there is no module.

reason.description: The reason, as the IR names it.

code.description: The code of the note it is reported with; null for one only a declaration can resolve, reported as a warning instead.

sinceLastRun.description: For generate, what changed since the output folder was last written; null for check and for a run that wrote nothing.

diagnostics.description: Everything the run found, in the order it found it: errors, warnings and every note, whatever --verbose or --quiet ask of the text; but for the warnings the config file acknowledges.

acknowledged.description: The warnings the config file's "acknowledge" names, each with its subject and why.

changes.description: Each change of claim, as check reports it.

kind.description: How the claim changed, such as became-nullable or values-added.

object.description: The object's id; empty for a claim of the whole document.

path.description: Where in the object, in the IR's path syntax; empty for the object itself.

before.description: The claim before, in words, when the kind needs it.

after.description: The claim after, in words, when the kind needs it.

text.description: The change as the text report writes it.

rewritten.description: The emitted files whose text changed though no claim did, or that the last run didn't write.

irRewritten.description: Whether the IR's text changed though no claim did: what it records of where its claims came from, or another version wrote it.

recorded.description: The script files whose text the IR records anew, by their hash: edited, or newly or no longer pointed into. The IR changes for each though no claim does.

why.description: Why there was nothing to compare with, as the text report says it.

diagnostic.$comment: An acknowledged warning has subject and why besides; they are named here so that additionalProperties allows them.

message.description: What is wrong and what to do; for a value in a JSON document, its path first, as the text report writes it.

file.description: The file it is in; null when it has no place.

line.description: The line, from 1; null when it has none.

column.description: The column, from 1; null when it has none.

subject.description: For an acknowledged warning, what it is about, as the config file names it.

why.description: For an acknowledged warning, why it is lived with.
